📋 Executive Summary

The robot operated safely within a simulated indoor environment, successfully navigating without any collisions or prohibited actor detections. The system reached the edge of its operational design domain by experiencing the full range of permissible lighting, from well-lit to dim. Although the robot's body tilt also neared its stability limit, this was identified as a simulation-specific anomaly and does not indicate a risk in real-world conditions.

Critical Axes: None
Rationale: The Current Operating Domain (COD) is at the boundary of the ODD. While no axes exceeded their limits (region_distance of 0.0), the 'lighting_conditions' axis operated in all three allowed states ('bright', 'moderate', 'dim'), exhausting its categorical margin and placing it at the boundary. The motion axis 'max_pitch_deg' was the closest numeric parameter to its limit, reaching 12.33° (ODD limit 15°), but remained within the required safety margin.

🔍 Key Findings

perception

The robot navigated a simulated indoor commercial space with hardwood and tile floors. Obstacle density was consistently low, peaking at only 3.2%. Lighting conditions varied significantly, covering the entire allowed range from 'bright' to 'dim', which was the primary driver of the boundary verdict.

motion

Robot dynamics were well-controlled, with a maximum speed of 0.28 m/s, far below the 1.5 m/s limit. A peak pitch of 12.33° was recorded, consuming 82% of the 15° ODD allowance, though this was flagged as a simulation artifact.

safety

No humans or animals were detected, and the system experienced no collisions. The 'lighting_conditions' axis operated with zero remaining margin by using all its allowed categories. The 'max_pitch_deg' axis had the smallest numeric margin at 17.8%.

temporal_trends

The system's performance was stable throughout the scenario. A temporary perception issue occurred in window w007, where a poor camera view led to a 'dim' lighting assessment and required reliance on LiDAR data. This event coincided with the observed peak in robot pitch.

⚠️ Issues Identified

  1. w007: Max pitch of 12.33° approached the 15° limit. Motion analysis identified this as a simulation artifact.
  2. w007: A perception anomaly occurred where the camera view was uninformative (unrendered simulation area), requiring full reliance on BEV/LiDAR data for environmental assessment.

💡 Recommendations

  1. Investigate the simulation physics engine to understand the cause of high pitch angles on flat terrain to improve simulation fidelity.
  2. Verify the perception system's robustness and fallback logic for scenarios where primary camera data becomes unavailable or unreliable, as observed in w007.
